title: State Preparation Protocols for Entangled States via Open Quantum Walks
abstract: Open quantum walks couple transitions on a graph to quantum operations on an internal degree of freedom. We use this structure to formulate protocols for quantum state preparation with nonunitary Kraus operators. We construct a ring-shaped OQW preparing an ensemble of Dicke states, with W states appearing as the single-excitation case, from which any individual Dicke state is recovered by postselecting the walker position; its convergence is governed by the spectral gap of the underlying Markov chain, for which we obtain a closed-form approximate expression. For GHZ states we present a two-node protocol using Kraus operators built from projective measurements that prepares them deterministically without requiring a measurement of the walker, and analyze how unsharp measurements affect the results and the convergence of the walk. We also show that the quantum trajectories method embeds naturally in the OQW framework as a graph-structured collision model.
summary: The paper introduces Open Quantum Walks (OQWs) as a powerful tool for designing protocols to prepare entangled states like Dicke and GHZ states. By coupling graph dynamics to internal qubits via engineered dissipation, it achieves deterministic preparation schemes even under imperfect measurements. This framework unifies quantum trajectory simulation with structured graph models.
main_problem: The paper develops protocols for preparing specific entangled quantum states (Dicke, W, GHZ) using the framework of Open Quantum Walks (OQWs). It aims to provide a general method applicable when state preparation relies on nonunitary dynamics.
main_result: Protocols are successfully constructed for Dicke and GHZ states; specifically, an OQW prepares an ensemble of Dicke states, and a two-node protocol deterministically generates GHZ states without requiring direct measurement of the walker's position.
method: The core method involves modeling dissipation and state evolution using Open Quantum Walks, which reformulates quantum trajectories via Kraus operators derived from engineered environmental coupling. Convergence rates are analyzed using spectral gap calculations.
model_or_system: The model is an OQW that couples transitions on a graph (the walker's position) to internal degrees of freedom representing the entangled state qubits. Specific topologies include ring-shaped graphs for Dicke states and simple two-node graphs for GHZ states.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F$) of prepared states, steady-state probabilities ($\pi_k$), and the spectral gap ($\Delta(\eta)$) governing convergence rates.
important_parameters: The degree of measurement sharpness ($\eta$), system size ($N$), and parameters related to dissipation/coupling strengths ($p, A$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes weak measurements or specific coupling structures (e.g., deriving operators from Lindblad forms). The method is shown to embed quantum trajectories but is not claimed to be a computational speedup.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the general OQW structure on graphs, show diagrams for linear and ring-shaped models, and detail the mathematical setup using transition operators derived from jump/Lindblad operators.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the OQW framework for state preparation, details specific protocols for Dicke states (using a ring graph) and GHZ states (using a two-node graph), analyzes convergence rates under measurement imperfections ($\eta$), and concludes by showing the natural embedding of quantum trajectories into this walk structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a physically transparent and general graphical framework (OQW) to analyze state preparation protocols, bridging concepts from open quantum systems theory with structured quantum information tasks like generating multipartite entanglement.
